description: mo:os ontology — aligned with foundation-t158.md. Grammar, not encyclopedia. 52 node types (+external_op), 20 rewrite categories (WF01-WF20). T=164 adds channel (media streams), purpose (directional intent), WF19 (session governance on kernels). T=166 adds channel.parent_channel_urn (folder nesting), tool_call.agent_urn (agent-as-tool wiring). T=167 adds system_instruction (S4, M7), transport_binding (S2, M10), session.local_t/context_urn (M1, M7). T=168 round-9 v3.10.0: D19.1 grammar_fragment merged — WF19 tgt_types extended with user and agent for §M19 session-occupancy. T=169 v3.11.0: t_hook gains firing_state lifecycle property (pending→proposed→approved|rejected→applied→closed). Plus baseline session type fixes: urn_pattern/description generalized to kernel-bound workspace semantics; seat_role deprecated under the single-driver-via-has-occupant-LINK model. See kb/research/session/20260419-t169-session-generalization.md. WF19 has-occupant tgt_types extends to include `group` (session occupancy by a collective principal). See kb/research/session/20260422-t172-wolframs-court-social-topology.md §3 + T=173 batch on Z440 kernel 0 log_seq 285-288 (WF20 promotion ceremony for the 4 fragments).

changelog.summary: First major bump (3.x -> 4.0). ALIAS-FIRST + ADDITIVE: no URN rewrite, no authority-model change, nothing existing removed or renamed. Lands the Sam-ratified (T=219) manifold-paradigm vocabulary. D1: `manifold` first-class S2 node-type, identity-first -- its spanning relations to instance/workspace/channel and their WF rewrite_category are DEFERRED to a follow-on fragment, exactly as v3.14 `derivation` landed before its WF21 LINKs. D2 `session`->`workspace` and D6 `kernel`->`instance` are ALIAS-FIRST labels only: canonical type-ids + URNs stay `session`/`kernel`; the hard ~59-site URN rewrite ships as a gated 4.0.x point release once Doctor + `go test ./...` pass. D3: `persona = Phi(purpose)` carried as a `derivation` convention (never an authority node). D5+D7 folded (P2): `channel.kind` += infra {domain, dns-zone, cloudflare-zone, cloudflare-tunnel, access-app, registrar, website-endpoint} + surface {workstation-surface, virtual-desktop, window, tab-group, browser-tab, harness-pane, keep-widget}. P1: `workstation.kind` enum {server, desktop, laptop, mobile, vm, edge} (retires the phantom `device` type). Runtime: ontology.json-only -- the operad loader is data-driven (new types/enums/properties/port-pairs load with zero Go change; enum values are inert/unchecked); moos-lsp symbols.go regenerated. Kernels must reload to serve 4.0.0.

changelog.summary: t_hook gains firing_state lifecycle. Replaces the v3.10 proposal-existence idempotency check; makes the firing contract legible as a state machine so the approver reactor can land cleanly.

property_additions: t_hook.firing_state — enum {pending, proposed, approved, rejected, applied, closed}. Default pending. Authority: kernel (only sweep/reactor transitions it). Transitions described in the property note.
contract_upgrades: Sweep filters on firing_state==pending (was: scan governance_proposal nodes to build an idempotency set). O(proposals) scan replaced by an O(1) per-hook predicate.
Sweep MUTATEs firing_state pending → proposed in the same ApplyProgram batch that ADDs the governance_proposal. Atomic transition; log-is-truth preserved.

Future approver reactor: governance_proposal.status pending → approved triggers firing_state proposed → applied (via react_template application). pending → rejected triggers firing_state proposed → rejected (terminal).
migration_actions_in_hg: Existing 10 t_hook nodes from round-8 have no firing_state property. At their first sweep evaluation under v3.11 kernel, an additive MUTATE sets firing_state → pending (the enum's default). This is a one-time no-op write per hook; idempotent under replay (ValidateMUTATE additive path accepts fields declared in the ontology spec).
No MUTATEs against ontology itself beyond the version+changelog bump.
backwards_compat: Pre-v3.11 kernels that don't know firing_state will tolerate the property (extra properties are allowed on ADD; kernel_validator rejects MUTATE on undeclared fields). A v3.10 kernel reading a v3.11 hook sees the firing_state as an extra property and ignores it, which means the old 'check proposal existence' idempotency still works. Rollback-safe.

invariants: ADD, LINK, MUTATE, UNLINK are the only four rewrites
P(delegate) <= P(principal) — permission inheritance, enforced at rewrite validation time (CI-5)

five_causal_invariants.CI1: Church-Rosser: M_a;M_b = M_b;M_a when affected(M_a) intersect affected(M_b) = empty
five_causal_invariants.CI2: Projection naturality (structure-preserving only): Project(Apply(M,S)) = Apply(M', Project(S)) for projections with declared rewrite correspondence
five_causal_invariants.CI3: Identity stability: forall M forall x: urn(M(x)) = urn(x)
five_causal_invariants.CI4: Log replay determinism: fold(log[0..t]) is deterministic — same log -> same state
five_causal_invariants.CI5: Rewrite category stability: permitted rewrite categories do not change under rewrites — only governance changes the operad

free_category_note.statement: The mo:os ontology is effectively the FREE category on its generators (types + WFs) — no equations are imposed beyond port_color_compatibility and permission inheritance (CI-5). Morphism equations such as WF composition laws, idempotence of specific MUTATEs, or commutativity of ADD+LINK sequences are NOT yet declared in this ontology.
free_category_note.implication: v3.9+ preserves freeness: new S1 types and WFs extend the generator set; any constraints must be ADDED as explicit invariants (not inferred from type shape). The S1-as-superset doctrine (see s1_superset_doctrine_reference) treats S1 as the free category on all patterns that any user or agent would formalize given sufficient observation.
free_category_note.future_work: Declare compose operator on WF pairs; spec morphism equations per-type; spec contract_schema (WF15) formally.

fold_contract.status: stub (v3.9) — full formalization deferred to T=187 sub-program (CI-4 formalization).
fold_contract.signature: fold : Log × InitialState → State, where fold([], s0) = s0 and fold(log ++ [r], s0) = Apply(r, fold(log, s0))
determinism_requirements: Apply(r, s) must be a pure function of (r, s) — no clock, randomness, network calls, filesystem reads.
Iteration order over relations must be deterministic (stable sort by urn or insertion order).
Any kernel-authority mutation (local_t, turn_count, status auto-transitions) must be derivable from the rewrite envelope alone, not from wall clock.
non_determinism_exclusions: Wall-clock T (the calendar day counter) — injected as envelope property at ADD time, never read inside Apply.
UUID generation — must be deterministic from envelope (hash of actor+target+seq).
External HTTP/DNS resolution — never performed inside Apply.
fold_contract.audit_note: Current kernel Apply respects these requirements by construction but they are not yet enforced by type-level checks. v3.10 candidate: per-WF fold_contract declaration.

use.node: identity point in graph (not: object, element, vertex)
use.relation: typed connection between nodes (not: binding, edge, wire, association)
use.rewrite: graph transformation operation (not: morphism for the op, update, mutation)
use.rewrite_category: family of allowed rewrites WF01-WF15 (not: named relation, UML association)
use.port: interface point on a node type (not: slot, endpoint)
use.operad: valid composition rules / type registry (not: schema, grammar)
use.property: typed key-value on a node (not: field, payload, attribute)
use.interaction_node: discrete interaction artifact node (not: transition, event, message)
use.manifold: top-category node (v4.0, D1) — an application/domain topology; the colimit of branch-episodes sharing one purpose-slug; e.g. manifold:my-tiny-data-collider
use.workspace: v4.0 alias of `session` (D2) — same node; canonical type-id/URN stay `session` until the gated 4.0.x rewrite
use.instance: v4.0 alias of `kernel` (D6) — `instance := fold(log)`, model-theoretic; canonical type-id/URN stay `kernel` until the gated 4.0.x rewrite
use.persona: v4.0 (D3) — a derived presentational identity `persona = Φ(purpose)`, carried as a `derivation`; NOT a node-type and never an authority principal

topology_property_boundary.rule: Relations are truth. Properties never duplicate topology.
topology_property_boundary.test: If the information involves two or more nodes, it is a relation (LINK/UNLINK). If it involves only one node's internal state, it is a property (MUTATE).
topology_property_boundary.exception: owner_urn and sender_urn are immutable provenance stamps set at ADD time. They reference another node but are NOT topology.

s2_infrastructure.description: The human principal. Exactly one user per kernel. Superadmin of their own graph.

Top-category node (v4.0, D1): an application/domain topology -- the durable locus where a group's domains, DNS, websites, instances/workspaces, and Workspace/GitHub/Calendar/tunnel channel-surfaces are facets of one topology. Categorically the colimit of the per-repo branch-episodes that share one purpose-slug. Sam-ratified T=219 as a new first-class category. Lands identity-first: its spanning relations (manifold -> instance / workspace / channel) and their WF rewrite_category are deferred to a follow-on fragment, exactly as the v3.14 `derivation` type landed before its WF21 LINKs. Worked example: manifold:my-tiny-data-collider.

owner_urn.note: provenance stamp, not topology -- the group/user this manifold belongs to

s2_infrastructure.note: Spanning relations to instances/workspaces/channels are NOT yet declared (no WF) -- follow-on fragment, per the migration guard. A Stage-1 derived view over group/purpose/session/channel data remains a valid read until those land.

s2_infrastructure.description: A running mo:os process. Sovereign — bound to one workstation, owned by one user.
s2_infrastructure.alias_note: 4.0 alias (D6): `instance` is the 4.0 label (instance := fold(log), model-theoretic sense). Canonical type-id and URN stay `kernel` until the gated 4.0.x rewrite. This field is doc-intent; no loader consumes it yet.

s2_infrastructure.description: A physical or virtual machine. Hosts kernels, contains compute and storage.

kind.note: Host-class discriminator (P1/D7). Retires the phantom `device` type -- every kind runs an instance at some F/G capability degree (server/desktop/laptop = full G-reach; mobile/edge = surface-heavy / reduced G-reach). Mutable+optional so existing workstation nodes backfill via an additive MUTATE.

s2_infrastructure.description: An AI delegate. Defined by properties and capabilities — not by IDE surface. Owned by one user.

invocation_protocol.note: How this agent is invoked at the application layer. Complements transport_type (wire-level protocol) and delegate_type (runtime kind). stdio = CLI agents / MCP stdio bindings; mcp = MCP SSE/Streamable-HTTP; http = plain HTTP endpoints. Promoted in the first WF20 ceremony (v3.12.0, T=169 round 10).

board_id.note: Short identifier used in GitHub project board Agent ID field. Convention: AGENT-<TOOL>-<WORKSTATION>. Bridges HG URN to external task-queue identity.

s2_infrastructure.note: Capabilities are discovered via WF02 relations to capability nodes — NOT stored as a property on this node (topology-property boundary rule).

s2_infrastructure.description: Persistent, always-on, kernel-bound workspace. Analogue: tmux session, Chrome tab, desktop application left open. Defined by the tuple (scope, purpose) × (host, owner, occupant): scope = pinned URNs (D19.3) + contained sessions (D22.5 future); purpose = single-valued has-purpose LINK (D22.1, promoted v3.16.0); host = the kernel it runs on (WF19 opens-on); owner = the principal served (user/agent/kernel-for-birth-sessions); occupant = the current driver (WF19 has-occupant, single-valued, rotatable via MUTATE target_urn). Not an IDE conversation — conversations are ephemeral and traced via actor_urn on each rewrite. See kb/research/session/20260419-t169-session-generalization.md for the full corrected model.
s2_infrastructure.alias_note: 4.0 alias (D2): `workspace` is the 4.0 label for this node. Canonical type-id and URN stay `session` until the gated 4.0.x rewrite. This field is doc-intent; no loader consumes it yet.

status.deprecation_note: Subsumed by seat_role + permanent-session model (§M11, §M18). Sessions are kernel-bound and never close — they transition to seat_role=observer. Kept for back-compat with existing instances; scheduled for removal in v3.10 along with role. See dev/reference/research-archive/20260418-t168-session-kernel-bound.md.

turn_count.deprecation_note: Subsumed by local_t (§M13 authoritative heartbeat). local_t is the kernel-maintained per-session rewrite counter; turn_count was never used by v3.8+ runtime. Scheduled for removal in v3.10.

local_t.note: Kernel-maintained per-session T counter (M1). Incremented automatically after each acknowledged rewrite issued within the session. Never decremented.

context_urn.note: URN of the system_instruction node (S4) providing context for this session (M7). Gates which WFs the session may exercise.

role.note: DEPRECATED (v3.9) — scheduled for removal in v3.10 after kernel validator honors seat_role. Live instances keep this value until MUTATEd to seat_role. Session role within kernel occupancy (WF19).

seat_role.deprecation_note: Redundant under the single-driver-via-has-occupant-LINK model (D19.1 merged v3.10, D22.2 invariant proposed v3.12). The presence/absence of the has-occupant LINK captures idle-vs-driven; the LINK target captures who. Observer/delegate semantics move to WF02 delegates-to LINKs between principals, orthogonal to session membership. Existing sessions carrying seat_role continue to validate until removal (scheduled v3.13). See kb/research/session/20260419-t169-session-generalization.md §3.

view_prefs.note: Scalar UI prefs held by the session for its occupant's t-cone rendering. Non-topological — anything topological (pins, filters) is carried by relations (D19.3/D19.4). Distinct from view_filter (a saved predicate): view_prefs is how the filtered result is displayed. Schema: {sort_by: enum[created_at|t_ref|target_t|priority], fold_depth: integer(default 2), density: enum[compact|comfortable|spacious], theme: string(optional)}.

s2_infrastructure.note: Participants are discovered via WF07 relations — NOT stored as a property. Each session is a category with one object (the session's snapshot); its self-morphisms (advance local_t, rotate has-occupant target_urn, rotate has-purpose, add/remove pin, mount/unmount tool, context-swap) form a monoid under composition with identity = no-op. §M4 `S: SessionCat → KernelCat` is the structure-preserving functor; WF19 is the naturality square. Two additional algebraic layers compose on top: operadic scope composition (sessions nest via scope containment, birth-session as root scope) and a user/group topology lattice orthogonal to scope (which principals can open/occupy which sessions, partially carried by WF02). The old 'session IS a monoid' phrasing (session-channel-purpose.md §2) confused identity-morphism with empty-object; the corrected framing lives in kb/research/session/20260419-t169-session-generalization.md §2. Sessions are PERMANENT kernel-bound S2 nodes — once WF19-LINKed (opens-on/occupied-by) to a kernel they persist indefinitely. A kernel's occupancy ledger is the set of has-occupant target_urns its session(s) have held over time, retrievable via log replay. Birth-session per kernel is ADDed atomically with the kernel (D22.4 proposed); additional purpose-scoped sessions may be ADDed as workspaces (Chrome-tab model). See §M11 (liveness), §M13 (local_t as heartbeat), §M18-§M20 (session generalization).

s2_infrastructure.description: A network interface: port + transport. Exposed by kernel, connected-to by agents.
A git repository. Part of the development infrastructure. Hosted on GitHub or local. Contains source code, ontology, or configuration.
A GitHub issue or task. Used as coordination unit between agents. Issues on the project board are the shared task queue. Status syncs with GitHub.

assignee_urn.note: Agent or user assigned. Provenance, not topology.

repo_urn.note: Which repository this issue belongs to. Provenance stamp.

s2_infrastructure.description: A computation substrate. CPU: sequential kernel spine. GPU: concurrent subgraph partitions as hypervector operations.
A persistent storage resource.
A request to promote a local contingent pattern to canonical. Human approval required.
A named bundle of permissions. Attached to delegates via WF02 relations.

builtin_roles.superadmin: all permissions — only principals hold this
builtin_roles.executor: read all, write code nodes and own session
builtin_roles.observer: read all, write own session and ack messages only
builtin_roles.hydrator: read kb, write S0-S2 nodes (ADD only)

s2_infrastructure.note: PERMISSION BUNDLE type (S1) — distinct from `session.role` (S2 enum: occupier|observer|delegate) which carries seat-state on a kernel. This is the permission-bundle role attached to a principal or delegate via WF02. Admin governance (§M12 in 20260417-t187-kernel-proper.md) binds: only a user whose WF02-bound role is `superadmin` may issue rewrites touching the ontology, ontology-governed types (system_instruction, gate, twin_link, transport_binding), or `authority_scope: kernel` property overrides. Enforcement: `operad.Validate` + M8 gate checks the actor's session's WF02 capabilities on every envelope; missing capability fails closed.

s2_infrastructure.description: Scoped permission token. Attached to delegate via WF02 relation. Constrains which rewrite categories the holder can request.

scope.note: list of WF categories this capability grants

s2_infrastructure.note: Per §M12 admin governance (20260417-t187-kernel-proper.md): every rewrite envelope is validated against the actor's session's WF02-bound capabilities at `operad.Validate`. Admin-scope rewrites (ontology edits, authority_scope:kernel fields, ontology-governed types) require a capability whose `scope` includes the relevant WF category — typically granted transitively via a `superadmin` role binding (S1). Missing capability: fails closed at the M8 gate.

s2_infrastructure.description: Program (PRG) — unit of work in mo:os. A branch of the multiway graph that receives runtime. Status lifecycle: planned → active → in_progress → completed | blocked.
s2_infrastructure.deprecation_note: Wave-0 legacy. New work uses `program` (v3.8+). Existing prg_task instances persist in the log; no destructive migration planned. See t168 audit §A6.

t_start.note: Moos-time T-day when PRG runtime began or is scheduled

s2_infrastructure.description: Program node — unit of purposeful work with temporal semantics. Replaces legacy prg_task for new work items. Temporal properties are forward-looking and mutable (plans shift). Dependencies can be known-node (LINK to specific URN) or property-pattern (watcher filter matching ANY node meeting conditions).

owner_urn.note: Provenance stamp — who created this program

scope.note: What this program delivers — mutable because scope evolves

target_t.note: Moos-time T-day target for completion. Mutable: plans shift.

starts_t.note: Moos-time T-day when work begins or is expected to begin

deadline_t.note: Hard deadline in Moos-time. Distinct from target_t (soft target).

completed_t.note: Moos-time T-day when status became completed. Set by MUTATE, not log timestamp.

s2_infrastructure.description: S2 node with S4-overlay role — human- or AI-authored instruction set that overlays the ontology (S1) read-only for a session (M7). Referenced by session.context_urn. Never modifies S0 directly; influence is through the session's WF scope gate. Gödel/Turing: may reference its own session — self-reference is typed (overlay ref → S2 occupier); incompleteness surfaces as gate failures, not crashes.
s2_infrastructure.stratum_clarification: v3.9 audit §B2: stratum is S2 (authored like any S2 node). Its S4-ness is a ROLE/overlay policy, not a stratum classification. Previous v3.8 declaration `stratum: S4` was inconsistent — the S4 projection layer is for read-only UI/filesystem sinks, not for first-class nodes referenced by S2 sessions. Cross-ref §M7 (kernel-proper) and 20260418-t168-v3.9-ontology-audit.md §B2.

wf_scope.note: WF categories the session is allowed to exercise when this instruction is active. Empty = no restriction.

s2_infrastructure.note: Stratum S4: projection only. A system_instruction is never ground truth — it is an overlay read by sessions to constrain their WF scope.

s2_infrastructure.description: Wire-level protocol binding for a kernel endpoint (M10). Captures whether an endpoint speaks HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, or HTTP/3-QUIC. Immutable once the kernel is live; migration is a new ADD + LINK. Alt-Svc header value is emitted by the kernel on every response to allow automatic upgrade.

listen_addr.note: TCP or UDP host:port the kernel listens on for this protocol

quic_addr.note: UDP host:port for QUIC listener (only set when protocol=http3-quic)

alt_svc.note: Value of the Alt-Svc header emitted on HTTP/1.1+HTTP/2 responses to signal QUIC availability

s2_infrastructure.description: Temporal anchor from Google Calendar. Bridges IRL time to Moos-time. Color-labeled events (purple = PRG-tracked) become graph nodes.
A persistent external source that produces knowledge items. YouTube channel, arxiv category, website RSS, API endpoint. Polled or pushed.

protocol.note: simple label; promote to protocol node via WF14 when capabilities matter

s2_infrastructure.description: A specific piece of content from a source feed. Video, paper, article, email thread. Extracted claims link to domain tags.

substrate.note: default hg-native; auto-defaulted on backfill for nodes minted pre-v3.15

substrate_anchor_urn.note: required when substrate in {external-channel, federation-reconciled}; resolves to channel|derivation that anchors the external observation

s2_infrastructure.description: An atomic assertion extracted from a knowledge item. The smallest unit of knowledge in the graph.

Reifies session-internal inference as a first-class graph object. Every program / claim / knowledge_item produced by a session can walk back to its derivation, the evidence consumed, the weights applied, and the confidence assigned. Closes the inference-visibility gap surfaced in T=175 program-authoring fabric note. Companion port-pair (authors-via/authored-by-session for session) deferred to a future fragment; for now derivation nodes ADD with all properties but their LINKs to programs/claims/evidence land via WF21 causes/caused-by once that fragment promotes. Added v3.14 per `urn:moos:grammar_fragment:v314-1-derivation-type`. v4.0 (D3): `persona = Φ(purpose)` is carried as a derivation — a reified session-internal inference of presentational identity from purpose/scope/affordance evidence; never an authority node (agents remain the operational principal). Provenance: purpose --WF21 causes--> the persona derivation.

name.note: short label for the derivation; e.g. glossary-h2-chunker

inference_kind.note: What kind of inference produced this derivation's outputs.

stochastic_weights.note: Free-form: priors, biases, temperature, top-p, sampling strategy, model_urn. Populated when inference_kind ∈ {bayesian, llm_completion, hybrid}; null/empty for deterministic_rule and hand_authored.

confidence.note: 0.0 to 1.0. 1.0 for deterministic_rule; varies for stochastic kinds.

status.note: open: derivation in flight; closed: emitted its outputs; retracted: superseded or withdrawn.

s2_infrastructure.description: Classification concept node. Linked to knowledge items and claims. Taxonomy source: arxiv, lcsh, or custom.
A formal classification system. Industry conventions, library standards, regulatory frameworks. The operad's alignment with real-world categories is checked through these nodes.

A mapping between two classification schemes OR between two crosswalks (higher-order). The graph-native witness of a natural transformation. Recursive: crosswalk-of-crosswalks encodes maps-between-maps (n-category depth). HDC-encodable at every level via binding.
Claude or agent session state — kernel snapshot, PRG focus, active connectors. Created at session start, mutated at end.
s2_infrastructure.deprecation_note: Merged into `session` per §M18 (session generalization). Wave-0 legacy. PRG-focus / connectors semantics migrate to session.view_prefs (v3.10). Port `reads` dropped (no matching in-port anywhere — audit §A5). Port `focus` retained on session (view/attention semantics). See t168 audit §A2, §A4, §A5.

s2_infrastructure.description: Presheaf on the rewrite log. Observes rewrites matching a pattern (type, port, URN prefix) and emits observations. Does NOT write — only watches.
s2_infrastructure.deprecation_note: Superseded by `t_hook` (§M14 T-hook predicate catalog). The watcher match fields (match_rewrite_type, match_type_id, match_urn_prefix, match_port) become a t_hook predicate of shape on_event / on_prop_set. Existing watcher instances continue to work through WF17 until migrated. See t168 audit §C.

match_type_id.note: node type_id to match, or * for any

match_port.note: port name to match on LINK/UNLINK, or empty

s2_infrastructure.description: Natural transformation: observation → proposed rewrite(s). Triggered by a watcher, emits rewrite envelopes for the kernel to validate and apply.
s2_infrastructure.deprecation_note: Superseded by `t_hook` (§M14 T-hook predicate catalog). The reactor template migrates to t_hook.react_template; action_type=rewrite|tool_call|notify maps into the hook's react contract. Existing reactor instances continue to work through WF17 until migrated. See t168 audit §C.

template.note: rewrite envelope template with {{placeholders}} filled from observation

s2_infrastructure.description: Subobject classifier: state predicate that gates a reactor. The reactor only fires if the guard evaluates true against current graph state.

negate.note: if true, guard passes when predicate is FALSE

s2_infrastructure.description: A named stream of messages, files, or posts. Groups externally-sourced artifacts (WhatsApp, Drive, filesystem, project board, mail) into a single topological entry point. Cooperadic: one channel emits many knowledge_items / message_packets. Source of ingested structure, not metadata. Added T=164.

kind.values_note: v4.0 (D5 infra + D7 surface, folded as P2): infra kinds domain..website-endpoint carry STRUCTURAL handles only in source_uri (never tokens/account-ids); surface kinds workstation-surface..keep-widget are S0 observed-not-authored projection substrate (never durable-store private window/tab contents). pip-window + compile-target deferred (B5).

source_uri.note: path, protocol URL, or external identifier — the ingress handle

parent_channel_urn.note: Parent channel for folder/hierarchy nesting. If set, this channel is a sub-channel of the referenced one. Enables filesystem folder structure and nested project boards without duplicating topology.

substrate.note: default hg-native; auto-defaulted on backfill for nodes minted pre-v3.15

substrate_anchor_urn.note: required when substrate in {external-channel, federation-reconciled}; resolves to channel|derivation that anchors the external observation

s2_infrastructure.note: Every node entering the kernel from an external source is WF12-linked to its channel. Channel is the cooperad upstream of ingestion.

s2_infrastructure.description: Directional intent. A declared target state that steers ongoing wiring. In HDC terms, φ(purpose) = φ(target_state) - φ(current_state) — a vector field on the graph topology. The reactive kernel can score candidate rewrites by cos(φ(rewrite_effect), φ(purpose)). Added T=164.

subject_urn.note: who declared the purpose — user or agent. Provenance stamp.

target_state.note: declared destination — prose now, node-set hypervector later

closed_at.note: set when status transitions to achieved or abandoned

s2_infrastructure.note: Purpose is not topology by itself — it becomes topology through WF18 (composition into programs/sessions). A session without a purpose is occupancy without direction.

s2_infrastructure.description: First-class t-hook port descriptor (M6). Owned by any node via owner_urn. The reactive engine fires react_template when a rewrite affects the owner and event_shape matches. Optional guard_ref gates the hook (fail-closed). Backwards-compatible with watcher/reactor/guard nodes -- both patterns coexist.

owner_urn.note: URN of the node this hook belongs to. Engine fires when that node is affected by a rewrite.

event_shape.note: JSON filter object: {rewrite_type, type_id, urn_prefix, port, field}. Omit or set to empty string / "*" to match any value on that dimension.

guard_ref.note: URN of an existing guard node. Empty string = no guard (hook always fires when shape matches). Missing guard node = fail closed.

react_template.note: Envelope template. Supports $matched_urn, $matched_type_id, $actor substitutions. Same format as reactor.template.

firing_state.note: Lifecycle of a firing attempt for this hook. v3.11 replaces the proposal-existence idempotency used by the sweep in v3.10. Transitions: pending (predicate not yet true) → proposed (sweep ADDed governance_proposal) → approved|rejected (admin MUTATE on proposal) → applied (approver reactor applied proposed_envelope) → closed (terminal, for expires_at-style hooks). The sweep filters on firing_state==pending so a hook won't re-fire once it's in any other state. kernel-authority because only the sweep/reactor mutate it — user edits would break the idempotency contract.

s2_infrastructure.description: Subobject classifier for incomplete data (M8). A gate node guards a target node via guards/guarded-by relation. When the kernel applies a rewrite to the guarded node, ALL linked gates are evaluated first. If any gate predicate fails, the rewrite is blocked (fail-closed). Gates check external data -- the predicate target_urn is typically a DIFFERENT node from the guarded one, avoiding circular self-reference. Distinct from guard nodes (WF17 reactive path): guards gate reactor proposals; gates block kernel Apply.

predicate_type.note: field_set: field must be present on target_urn (any value). node_property: field must equal expected_value. node_exists / relation_exists: structural check.

target_urn.note: URN of the node the predicate checks. Typically DIFFERENT from the guarded node (avoid circular self-reference).

field.note: Property field name for node_property and field_set predicates.

negate.note: If true, the predicate result is inverted.

s2_infrastructure.description: Adjoint sync pair between two kernels (M9). Captures F ⊣ G: local kernel K forwards rewrites to remote K' via F (eager POST to remote_endpoint/twin/ingest); K' acknowledges back via G. sync_mode controls direction: eager = local pushes to remote; read-only = local only receives; lazy = batched (future). Loop prevention: configure at most one side as eager; the other as read-only.

remote_urn.note: URN of the remote twin kernel.

remote_endpoint.note: HTTP base URL of the remote kernel (e.g. https://kernel.my-tiny-data-collider.nl). POST /twin/ingest is appended.

sync_mode.note: eager: forward every rewrite immediately via POST /twin/ingest. read-only: receive only (no forwarding). lazy: batch (future).

s2_infrastructure.description: Saved predicate/filter a session uses as its t-cone (§M15) lens. Reuses §M14 t-hook predicate algebra (fires_at / closes_at / window / after_urn / recurs_every / on_event / on_prop_set / when_capability / ... with all_of / any_of composition). Multiple sessions can share a named filter. Added v3.9 per audit §D1. Supports §M18 session-as-workspace-anchor.

predicate.note: §M14-algebra predicate. Top-level `filter_type: all_of | any_of` wraps a list of predicates. Each predicate has a `predicate_type` from the M14 catalog and its own fields.

s2_infrastructure.audit_note: Port pair `filters-session / filtered-by` is declared in v3.9 but WF20 (grammar_promotion) may also use it; the kernel validator should accept the pair via WF18 composition rules until a dedicated WF21 session-view-composition is specified (deferred).

s2_infrastructure.description: Running execution environment for agents or tools. Generalizes prg_task.harness_pattern enum (fixed-plan-sequential | dynamic-plan-adaptive) into a first-class S2 node that can be MUTATEd and LINKed. A harness hosts agent processes, provides tool invocation surface, and carries resource bounds. Added v3.9 per audit §D6.

harness_pattern.note: Execution shape. Extends the v3.8 prg_task.harness_pattern values with runtime-shape variants (stdio-tool, mcp-tool, http-service).

invocation_surface.note: Structural description of how agents/tools are invoked within this harness (e.g. stdin/stdout schema, MCP server URN, HTTP base URL).

resource_bounds.note: CPU/RAM/GPU/timeout bounds. Optional. Enforcement out of scope for v3.9.

s2_infrastructure.audit_note: Sub-program t187.tool-mounting (§M20) uses harness to ground the `mounts-tool` relation. v3.10 candidate: add benchmark/evaluation types paired with harness for §D7/§D8.

s2_infrastructure.name: Group (collective principal)
s2_infrastructure.description: Collective principal — multiple users, agents, or mixed entities sharing ownership/occupancy scope. Mirrors GitHub organization-team semantics. Extends principalTypes in §M12 admin chain to {user, agent, group}. Seats that need delegation to a named collective reify as group nodes with member-of relations inbound and owns/delegates-to outbound. CheckAdminCapability in operad/occupancy.go can hop through group membership if actor is in a group that holds WF02 governs → role:superadmin. v3.13 addition from grammar_fragment v313-7-group-type.

owner_urn.note: sticky provenance; who ADDed the group

s1_grammar.description: Network endpoint for a kernel or router. Carries connection details. Linked to kernel via WF05 (exposes). v3.9 rename from S1 `endpoint` — resolved collision with S2 `endpoint` type. No live instances of S1 endpoint existed at time of rename (non-breaking in practice).
URN prefix routing rule: maps a URN prefix to a kernel_instance. The router reads these to decide where to forward rewrites.
The cocone/gateway that routes rewrites and queries to kernel instances based on shard_rules. One router can serve multiple kernels.
An S0-S4 classification layer. First-class so the graph can reason about its own strata.

instances.name: authored
instances.description: Human-written seeds, design docs, industry data

instances.name: evaluated
instances.description: Concurrent subgraph eval: hypervector encoding, ranking

instances.name: projected
instances.description: UI, filesystem, API — NEVER ground truth

s1_grammar.description: Named competence a user or agent declares. Distinct from `capability` (which is a permission token): a skill is `I know how to do X`; a capability is `I am allowed to do X`. Skills are S1 because they form the vocabulary for capability declarations and for occupant<->tool binding (§M20). Added v3.9 per audit §D2.

taxonomy_source.note: Industry taxonomies pre-registered — `custom` for user-authored skills.

s1_grammar.description: A proposed extension to S1 — a candidate type, port, or WF clause — authored at S4 (system_instruction) or S2 (governance_proposal) and promoted via WF20. Carrier of the S4→S1 adjoint `Promote`. Status lifecycle: proposed → (rejected | promoted | merged). Merged fragments are folded into the next ontology.json baseline version. See s1_superset_doctrine_reference for the full adjoint pattern. Added v3.9 per audit §D3.

fragment_kind.note: What kind of S1 object this fragment proposes.

specification.note: Structured spec matching fragment_kind: e.g. for type, a partial type descriptor (id, stratum, ports, properties). For port, a port_color + direction + allowed pairings. For wf_clause, src_types/tgt_types/mutate_scope patch.

evidence_urns.note: S4 nodes (system_instruction) or S2 nodes (governance_proposal) cited as evidence of the recurring pattern.

status.note: proposed → admin review → rejected | promoted (enters next ontology draft) | merged (applied to ontology baseline and version bumped).

rejection_reason.note: Populated when status=rejected. Used by v3.10 re-proposal gate (deferred: blocked_until).

s1_grammar.audit_note: v3.9 leaves evidence aggregation algorithm and automated pattern detection deferred. v3.9 only gives the nouns and WF20 verb; humans still author governance_proposals and promote them. Open questions per s1_superset_doctrine_reference §Open questions (embedding calculation, adjoint verification, rejection semantics).

s1_grammar.description: First-class template class. Generalizes t_hook.react_template and reactor.template. A pattern is a parameterized rewrite or structural template that can be instantiated into a concrete rewrite envelope by substituting placeholders with runtime values. Added v3.9 per audit §D4.

template.note: The parameterized template. {{placeholders}} are substituted at instantiation time. For rewrite_template: a partial rewrite envelope. For structural_template: a subgraph shape. For predicate_template: a §M14-algebra predicate with free variables.

placeholders.note: Named placeholders the instantiator must bind. E.g. [source_urn, target_type].

s1_grammar.description: Executable process template — DAG-shaped composition of rewrite steps, tool invocations, or sub-workflows. Distinct from WF rewrite categories (WF01..WF20). A workflow node is a first-class reified process that a session can instantiate and execute step-by-step. Added v3.9 per audit §D5.

dag.note: DAG spec: nodes = steps (rewrite | tool_call | sub_workflow_urn), edges = data/control dependencies. Topological execution order enforced at run.

s1_grammar.audit_note: v3.9 declares workflow as an S1 generator; runtime (workflow execution engine) is NOT specified in v3.9. Relationship to `program` (S2 unit-of-purposeful-work): a program INSTANTIATES a workflow, not vice versa. Relationship to `harness` (S2): a workflow runs IN a harness.

agent_urn.note: If this tool call invokes an agent (agent-as-tool pattern), references the agent node being called. Enables clean wiring: tool_call → LINK(WF05) → agent without encoding the relation in a property.

interaction_nodes.description: IRL-condition gate node (§M17 S2 type). A manual operation that must be performed before an automated kernel path can proceed. Visible in the t-cone as pending action items with deadline_t. Each external_op carries a command_hint for the operator and automates_via_urn pointing at the program it unblocks. Status lifecycle is kernel-observed actuator state: pending → done | cancelled.

status.note: Kernel-observed actuator lifecycle. owner_urn remains provenance/control; status closeout is emitted by the kernel or an admin-authorized runtime path after evidence exists.

deadline_t.note: Moos-time T-day by which this operation must be completed.

command_hint.note: Shell command or procedure hint for the operator.

responsible_urn.note: URN of the user or agent responsible for executing this operation.

automates_via_urn.note: URN of the program or sub-program this external_op unblocks when done.

interaction_nodes.audit_note: Added T=168 round 8. Models IRL-gate conditions (ssh, DNS, curl) that must complete before twin-deploy-mtdc or v310-delivery can proceed. Proposed as grammar_fragment pending formal WF linkage.

port_color_compatibility.description: Which source→target port color pairs produce valid relations. Any pair not listed is rejected at validation time.
port_color_compatibility.projection_rule: projection ports are read-only S4 sinks — never source of truth, never form causal relations
port_color_compatibility.semantic_rule: semantic ports (WF15) may compose with any color only when contract_urn is provided

declared_pairs_by_wf.note: agent->repository: agent works in this repo

declared_pairs_by_wf.constraint: contract_urn required — channel's kind declares the emission contract

ci2_projection_registry.description: Registry of CI-2 compliant structure-preserving projections. Projections not listed here are lossy — valid for S4 display only, not for authority.

ci2_compliant.definition: All properties of one specific node
ci2_compliant.corresponding_M_prime: MUTATE same field on projected record

ci2_compliant.definition: Agent node + all mutable property values
ci2_compliant.note: Compliant only for MUTATE — not for ADD/UNLINK of unrelated nodes

ci2_compliant.definition: Set of all WF07 relations incident to a session
Set of all WF02 relations from agent to capability nodes
Set of all WF05 relations from kernel to endpoint nodes
Ordered list of all logged rewrites for a kernel

lossy.reason: Aggregate; no M' — many rewrites can produce same delta or cancel
Time-ordered display; insertion doesn't commute with ranking
Many-to-one: same display from different graph states
Filesystem layout != graph topology; multiple S4 views possible
Joins and computed fields have no natural M'

s4_cache_contract.description: Rules governing when and how S4 denormalization caches may exist.

allowed_caches.name: agent_capabilities_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF02 LINK or UNLINK on that agent

allowed_caches.name: session_participants_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF07 LINK or UNLINK on that session

allowed_caches.name: kernel_endpoints_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF05 LINK or UNLINK on that kernel

allowed_caches.name: agent_properties_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF02 MUTATE on that agent

forbidden_patterns: capability_urns property on agent node — topology stored as property
participant_urns property on session node — topology stored as property
port_urns property on kernel node — topology stored as property
any S4 cache read by rewrite validator
any S4 cache used to initialize ADD/LINK source

rewrite_categories.name: Ownership
rewrite_categories.description: Principal owns workstation, kernel, or storage.

additional_port_pairs.description: Generalized ownership port-pair. Lifts the ownership relation from property (owner_urn, scattered across every node type) to typed topology. Coexists with the primary owns/child pair (legacy user→workstation) and also with owner_urn properties (sticky provenance) — operads can derive owner_urn from inbound owned-by edges when needed, deprecating the property gradually. Enables group→downstream traversal (what does group:sam own?).

rewrite_categories.name: Governance
rewrite_categories.description: Principal governs delegate with delegated role and capabilities.

additional_port_pairs.description: Role→role capability delegation. A superadmin role can narrow-delegate scoped sub-capability to other roles (e.g. role:superadmin --delegates-to--> role:karpathy-scope, role:steinberger-scope, role:moos-scope). operad.CheckAdminCapability can extend to traverse delegates-to up to a bounded depth so scoped roles inherit narrowed admin capability without requiring full superadmin assignment. v3.13 addition from grammar_fragment v313-6.

rewrite_categories.name: Hosting
rewrite_categories.description: Workstation hosts a kernel.

rewrite_categories.name: Containment
rewrite_categories.description: Workstation contains compute or storage.

rewrite_categories.name: Exposure
rewrite_categories.description: Kernel exposes a network endpoint.

rewrite_categories.name: Connection
rewrite_categories.description: Agent connects to a kernel endpoint or repository. For repositories: expresses that this agent works in / has access to that repo.

rewrite_categories.name: Workflow lifecycle
rewrite_categories.description: Participation, focus, anchoring, and status changes across sessions, PRGs, and calendar events. The workflow-colored WF.

additional_port_pairs.description: Calendar G-ingest source anchor. A calendar_event observation may anchor back to the graph node it projects or observes; target type is wildcard because source_urns can be claims, derivations, sessions, agents, groups, grammar fragments, programs, knowledge_items, or other reviewed node types.

rewrite_categories.name: Substrate binding
rewrite_categories.description: Compute or storage is physically bound to workstation.

rewrite_categories.name: Compute attachment
rewrite_categories.description: Kernel routes operations to compute substrates.

rewrite_categories.name: Persistence
rewrite_categories.description: Kernel's rewrite log persists in a storage resource.

rewrite_categories.name: Sync
rewrite_categories.description: Local storage syncs to/from a remote storage.

rewrite_categories.name: KB provision and hydration
rewrite_categories.description: Knowledge base provision: storage→kernel boot hydration, source_feed→knowledge_item production, channel→knowledge_item/message_packet ingestion, knowledge_item→claim extraction, tagging to domain_tags, and classification via scheme/crosswalk nodes.

rewrite_categories.name: Promotion
rewrite_categories.description: Governance proposal targets storage/kernel for canonicalization.

rewrite_categories.name: Implementation
rewrite_categories.description: Agent, kernel, or endpoint implements a protocol, language, capability, runtime, or package.

rewrite_categories.name: Semantic (open)
rewrite_categories.description: Open semantic relation. Allowed only with explicit port names AND a contract_schema reference.
rewrite_categories.constraint: No untyped semantic relations — contract_schema required
rewrite_categories.audit_note: v3.9 audit §B4: description and mutate_scope reference `contract_schema` but no such type exists in the ontology. v3.9 leaves this as a descriptive placeholder — `contract_schema` is a v3.10 candidate type. Current WF15 usage in production is nil; validator rejects all untyped semantic LINKs which is the intended behavior. Relationship to `classification_scheme` (S2, existing taxonomy type): classification_scheme is about WHAT is being classified (e.g. LCC/Dewey), contract_schema would be about HOW a semantic relation is typed. Distinct concepts. Do not rename.

rewrite_categories.name: Federation
rewrite_categories.description: Routing and connectivity for distributed kernel instances. Router reads shard_rules to route rewrites. Kernels expose endpoints. Shard_rules map URN prefixes to kernel instances.

rewrite_categories.name: Reactive
rewrite_categories.description: Watch/React/Guard pipeline. Watchers observe the rewrite log, trigger reactors when patterns match. Guards gate reactors with state predicates. The firestarter on the carpet.
rewrite_categories.note: Reactive rules are per-kernel — they observe the local log, not remote kernels

rewrite_categories.name: Program composition
rewrite_categories.description: Wires program nodes to their constituent tasks, outputs, sessions, purposes, and sub-programs. Temporal dependency DAG. Known-node dependencies use LINK directly; property-pattern dependencies use WF17 watchers that fire when ANY node matching a filter achieves required properties.

rewrite_categories.name: Session governance
rewrite_categories.description: Opens, maintains, transfers, and closes session occupancy of kernels by agent delegates. Session is a monoid over kernel occupancy: empty session is identity, sequential claims compose. WF19 gates occupancy against WF02 capability scope (a delegate cannot open a session on a kernel whose owner's capability does not grant required WF categories). Complements WF07, which tracks participation; WF19 tracks kernel OCCUPANCY. Sovereign by kernel — sessions are local-only. Added T=164.

additional_port_pairs.description: §M19 session-occupancy port pair. Session holds at-most-one has-occupant relation at a time pointing at the user or agent that is currently driving the session. Rotation = MUTATE of the LINK's target_urn (atomic; preserves session identity per CI-3). D22.2 (proposed v3.12) formalizes the at-most-one invariant. Zero has-occupant = session alive but idle; one = session occupied and driving. (v3.13: tgt_types extends with `group` — a session can have a collective principal as occupant via group-as-occupant.)

§M18 session workspace anchor — pins. Session pins arbitrary nodes (kernels, programs, purposes, other sessions, knowledge_items, calendar_events — any node) as its follow-list / dashboard contents. Many pins per session (unlike has-occupant which is single-valued). Adding a pin = ADD pins-urn LINK; removing = UNLINK. Workspace scope evolves via topology changes, not via property churn.

§M18 session workspace anchor — filtered view. Session binds to one or more view_filter nodes whose predicates restrict what's visible in the t-cone projection. §M15 t-cone composes as the intersection over all bound predicates. Multiple view_filters allowed per session.

§M20 session workspace anchor — mounted tools. Session binds to agent nodes that the session's occupant can invoke under WF02 capability scope. Multiple mounted tools per session allowed. Distinguishes the session's invokable-tools-list (topology) from its occupant (who is actually driving right now). When combined with agent.invocation_protocol (v3.12) this gives the session a full tool-library shape compatible with MCP client, LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.

§M-purpose session has-purpose anchor. Session has at most one active purpose at any instant; repurposing = MUTATE of the LINK target_urn (atomic; preserves session identity per CI-3). Reifies the session's why as a typed graph edge instead of routing through WF18 program composition. Round-10 doctrine seed; promoted T=185 round-16 ceremony.

rewrite_categories.note: WF19 is gated by WF02: capability.scope must include the WF categories the delegate will exercise. local_t and context_urn are kernel-authority fields mutated automatically. v3.9: mutate_scope adds `seat_role` alongside legacy `role` — both supported; removal of the legacy `role` field is scheduled for v3.11. v3.10.0: D19.1 grammar_fragment merged — tgt_types extended with user and agent, plus an additional port pair (`has-occupant` / `is-occupant-of`) to carry occupancy topology. The canonical pair (`opens-on` / `occupied-by`) remains the session-to-kernel seat link; the additional pair is session-to-principal, used by §M15 t-cone for capability resolution. Kernel support (port-color mapping + occupant/admin helpers) lands in the companion moos-kernel PR #13 — this ontology bump is the ffs0-side half. v3.12.0: first WF20 ceremony promotes D19.3 (pins-urn/pinned-by-session → any node, many pins), D19.4 (filtered-by/filters-session → view_filter), and D20.1 (mounts-tool/tool-mounted-in-session → agent) as three new additional_port_pairs — completing the §M18-§M20 session-as-workspace shape. seat_role property deprecated under the corrected single-driver-via-LINK model (see kb/research/session/20260419-t169-session-generalization.md §3). NOTE TO KERNEL CODE: the current operad/loader.go does not consume additional_port_pairs; the five pairs declared here (has-occupant plus the three v3.12 additions) validate only as the primary opens-on/occupied-by pair until the loader gains multi-port-pair awareness. Tracked as a code gap; round-11 session-occupancy sub-program closes it.

rewrite_categories.name: Grammar promotion
rewrite_categories.description: Carries the S4→S1 adjoint `Promote` functor. Admin-authored rewrites that ADD grammar_fragment nodes citing S4 (system_instruction) or S2 (governance_proposal) evidence, then MUTATE their status (proposed → rejected | promoted | merged). When a fragment reaches status=merged, the next ontology baseline version bumps and the fragment's specification is folded into the canonical ontology. Added v3.9 per audit §F and s1_superset_doctrine_reference.
rewrite_categories.audit_note: v3.9 DOES NOT auto-propose grammar_fragments from observed patterns — humans still author them. The adjoint is a design principle, not an algorithm yet. Open questions (evidence aggregation thresholds, re-proposal gating, embedding-based pattern similarity via HDC) tracked in s1_superset_doctrine_reference. Unit/counit laws (round-trip coherence Promote∘Express, Express∘Promote) are ASSERTED but not mechanically verified in v3.9.

rewrite_categories.name: causes
rewrite_categories.validator_extension: ValidateCausalAcyclic — reject any LINK that would close a cycle in the causes/caused-by DAG
